intro: You're looking for a protection financial adviser near you because you want to make sure your family would be financially secure if something happened to you. Protection advisers recommend life insurance, income protection and critical illness cover, and they can help you understand which type of cover might suit your circumstances. The right adviser will explain the options clearly and help you put protection in place.
need_heading: What people searching for protection advice usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a protection adviser want to protect their family or their income from the unexpected.
needs: You have a mortgage or rent to pay and want to make sure your family could keep up the payments if you died or became too ill to work.
You have children and want to ensure there would be money to cover everyday living costs if you were no longer around.
You are self-employed or your employer does not offer sick pay, so you need income protection to cover your bills if illness or injury stopped you working.
You have a health condition or a family history of illness and want to understand how that might affect your cover and what an insurer would need to know.
You already have some cover through work or a previous policy and want to check whether it is enough or whether you need to add to it.
context_heading: What to understand about protection advice
context: Protection advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Before you use an adviser, check on the FCA register that they are authorised or are an appointed representative of an authorised firm. If something goes wrong, you can complain to the firm and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.

Advisers must tell you whether their advice is independent (considering the whole market) or restricted (limited to certain products or providers), and how they charge. Advanced qualifications such as Chartered status from the Chartered Insurance Institute or the Personal Finance Society, or certifications like CFP, show that an adviser has met higher professional standards. It is worth asking about these when you speak to someone.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for a protection financial adviser near you, so we can introduce you to someone who covers your area.
Explain who you want to protect, for example your partner, children or other dependants, and what you want the cover to achieve.
Say whether you already have any protection policies in place, such as life insurance through work or a personal policy.
Describe your health situation briefly, including any existing conditions or family history that might be relevant to underwriting.
Mention whether you have a mortgage or other debts that you want the protection to cover.
Let us know if you have a preference for independent or restricted advice, or if you would like the adviser to explain the difference.
questions: Are you independent or restricted, and what does that mean for the protection products you can recommend?
How do you charge for your advice, and will you tell me the cost before I commit?
What information will you need about my health and lifestyle, and how will that affect the underwriting?
Should the policy be written in trust, and what difference would that make to a payout?
What happens if my circumstances change, such as if I change jobs or have a child?
Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and can you provide your firm's reference number?

faqs.q: What is the difference between independent and restricted protection advice?
faqs.a: Independent advisers consider the whole market when recommending protection products, while restricted advisers are limited to certain products or providers. Advisers must tell you which type of advice they offer before you proceed, so you can decide what suits you.

faqs.q: Why does my health matter for protection cover?
faqs.a: Insurers assess the risk you present, so your health and medical history can affect whether you are offered cover and on what terms. Underwriting is a normal part of the process, and an adviser can help you understand what information you will need to provide.

faqs.q: Should I put my protection policy in trust?
faqs.a: Writing a policy in trust can help ensure that a payout goes to the people you intend without delay, and it may have inheritance tax benefits. An adviser can explain whether a trust is suitable for your situation.

faqs.q: How often should I look at my protection cover again?
faqs.a: It is a good idea to go over your cover after major life changes such as moving house, having a child, changing jobs or getting married. An adviser can help you check whether your existing cover still meets your needs.

extra_heading: What 'near me' means for protection advice
extra: Protection advice rarely needs someone to visit your home, so 'near me' is often more about finding an adviser you feel comfortable speaking to than about distance. Many advisers work by phone or video as well as in person, so someone a little further away may still suit you well.

It helps to think about why local matters to you. If you would rather sit down face to face, say so when you enquire, and mention how far you are willing to travel. If convenience is the main thing, an adviser who covers your area but works remotely could be just as good.

When you compare the advisers you are introduced to, ask the same questions of each: whether their advice is independent or restricted, how they charge, and what qualifications they hold. That way you can judge the options on the things that actually affect the advice you receive.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to meet a protection adviser in person?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many people are happy to discuss life insurance, income protection and critical illness cover by phone or video, and some advisers work this way as standard. If meeting face to face matters to you, mention it when you enquire so we can take it into account.

extra_faqs.q: Does it cost anything to be introduced through iComply?
extra_faqs.a: iComply is a free introduction service: you tell us what you need and we introduce you to a suitable UK professional, who quotes you directly. Any fee for the advice itself is set by the adviser and is on application, so ask them to explain their charges before you go ahead.
